item.title: Resolving the heart of the Wolf-Rayet binary Apep with ALMA
item.description: arXiv:2610.22406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Wolf-Rayet (WR) phase is a critical stage in the evolution of massive stars. During this phase, the stars experience a large mass loss in the form of fast winds that are enriched with heavy elements. There are only a few WR binaries in the galaxy, with Apep being a truly exceptional system exhibiting a bright colliding-wind region at radio wavelengths and an impressive dust plume in the infrared. Although the angular separation between the two (WN and WC) components has been indirectly inferred to be about 47 mas, it has yet to be confirmed through direct measurements. We aim to image the Apep system at millimetre wavelengths to determine the position of the WR stars and their mass-loss rates. We observed Apep with ALMA in Bands 6 and 7 in a large baseline configuration, achieving an angular resolution of approximately 20 mas. We used a canonical spherical wind model to convert the measured flux densities into wind mass-loss rates. Towards Apep, we detect point-like emission coming from the WN star and elongated emission most likely from the colliding-wind region; the WC star is not detected. We also detect the O star at 0.7'' that has been associated with the system. Our analysis favours mass-loss rates for the WN and WC components of $\dot{M}_\mathrm{WN}\sim 2\times10^{-5}\,M_\odot \,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ and $\dot{M}_\mathrm{WC}\sim10^{-5}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, respectively. The mass-loss rates of the WR stars are significantly lower than previously reported, and we examine several factors that may account for this discrepancy. The diffuse emission from the colliding-wind region cannot be accounted for by the synchrotron flux, and thus additional free-free or dust emission is present.
item.dc:creator: S. del Palacio, W. Vlemmings, M. Fern\'andez-L\'opez, M. De Becker, P. Benaglia, V. Bosch-Ramon, B. Marcote, Luis A. Zapata

item.title: Discovery of eclipses in the cataclysmic variable MASTER OT J232100.42+494614.0
item.description: arXiv:2610.22443v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I performed photometric observations of the poorly studied cataclysmic variable MASTER OT J232100.42+494614.0 and discovered eclipses. I observed nine eclipses over two groups of closely spaced nights, separated by a 12-month interval. I precisely calculated the orbital period of the system to be Porb=0.212371533+\-0.000000069 days. For the eclipses, I created an ephemeris that is accurate for a long time span and suitable for analysing changes in the orbital period. The star's brightness outside of the eclipses varied between 15.61+\-0.02 and 18.04+\-0.05 mag. As the brightness decreased, the eclipses became more profound whereas its width remained unchanged. The average depth of eclipses was 1.36+\-0.03 mag, and the average width at half-depth was 0.0512(15) phases. I calculated the possible inclination of the orbit to be between 72.8 and 76.3 degrees, and the range of the average absolute V-band magnitude of the disc to be between 6.37+\-0.35 and 6.68+\-0.35 mag. Although the light curve of MASTER OT J232100.42+494614.0 from the ZTF survey showed insufficiently large outbursts with amplitudes less than 2.5 mag, it should be classified as a dwarf nova, as the average disc brightness and mass transfer rate are below the threshold for thermal instability.
item.dc:creator: V. P. Kozhevnikov

item.title: Let Sleeping Stars Li: Mapping Turnoff Lithium, the Lithium Dip, & Testing Standard Model Predictions in GALAH DR4 Subgiants
item.description: arXiv:2610.22492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lithium is an excellent tracer of stellar mixing. We reconstruct the end of the main sequence lithium depletion pattern using the GALAH DR4 3D-NLTE lithium dataset for 22,442 stars, complemented by masses and subgiant lithium dilution factors inferred from YREC stellar models. We recover the two canonical features seen in clusters: a cool plateau ($\mathrm{M_{[Fe/H]_{\odot}}} \sim 1.2 \mathrm{M_\odot}$) with a median $A(Li) = 2.42$, and a steep plunge into the lithium dip ($\mathrm{M_{[Fe/H]_{\odot}}} \sim 1.35 \mathrm{M_\odot}$) dominated by upper limits at $A(Li) < 1.5$. Above the dip, our data reveal a striking new pattern with a wide range of abundances. We argue this reflects severe rotationally induced mixing in most stars, with lithium preserved in a minority where gravitational settling suppresses mixing. Lithium depletion with intrinsic dispersion is universal across the sample. Predicted and observed dilution trends agree well below the dip. For higher-mass stars, dilution corrections agree with standard models, but our upper envelope lies below open cluster values. We attribute this to a shallower lithium preservation zone and further evidence for gravitational settling and radiative levitation. We detect lithium in $\approx25\%$ of dip stars, whereas clusters show none; neither blurring of a narrow mass feature nor binary contamination fully explains this. The cool plateau is 0.8 dex below the solar meteoritic value across a wide range of $[Fe/H]$. After accounting for pre-main sequence depletion, the plateau is elevated at $\geq [Fe/H]_{\odot}$, possibly evidence for lithium production.
item.dc:creator: Vincent A. Smedile, Marc H. Pinsonneault

item.title: Searching for Dwarf Novae in 47 Tucanae
item.description: arXiv:2610.22587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The globular cluster 47 Tucanae has 43 strong cataclysmic variable candidates, four of which are confirmed dwarf novae. Tidal capture theory predicts the existence of dozens of dwarf novae, suggesting more are undiscovered. Using 435 nm and 475 nm long exposure images from Hubble's ACS camera, we searched five epochs of archival Hubble images and did not find any variability at the scale of a dwarf nova eruption. We found 1 previously undiscovered variable object on the main sequence that could not be classified as a CV; the object experienced a change of approximately 0.3 Mag in 425 nm, and 0.2 mag in 635 nm over the course of 12 days. The lack of new CV detections in 47 Tucanae could be a result of the short timescale of the DN eruption, and a low observing probability. However, this null result may also support research suggesting most CVs in globular clusters are not dynamically formed, and tidal capture theory overestimates the detectable CV population.
item.dc:creator: Iman Behbehani, Michael Shara, David Zurek

item.title: Double Trouble: How Unresolved Spectroscopic Binary Stars Skew GALAH DR4 Stellar Parameters
item.description: arXiv:2610.22707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Unresolved binary stars introduce systematic biases in stellar parameter estimates when analysed assuming a single star. Using $\sim$917{,}000 spectra from the Galactic Archaeology with HERMES (GALAH) Data Release 4 (DR4), we develop a binary spectral model that fits each observed spectrum as the superposition of two synthetic spectra generated from the same model architecture used by GALAH DR4. These generative spectral models take as input: effective temperature ($T_\mathrm{eff}$), surface gravity ($\log g$), iron abundance ([Fe/H]), projected rotation velocity ($v \sin i$), microturbulence velocity ($v_\mathrm{mic}$), and radial velocity ($v_\mathrm{rad}$). In our binary model, $T_\mathrm{eff}$ and $\log g$ are not fitted directly but are instead interpolated from PARSEC isochrones based on stellar mass and age, under the assumption that both components formed contemporaneously with the same compositions. We fit for the primary and secondary masses, a common age and [Fe/H], as well as individual $v \sin i$, $v_\mathrm{mic}$, and $v_\mathrm{rad}$ for each component. After iterative optimization and conservative quality cuts to ensure robust detections, we identify $\sim$12{,}911 candidate binary systems. We quantify typical biases introduced by unresolved binarity: $T_\mathrm{eff}$ shifts of $-142$ to $+200$ K, $\log g$ shifts of $-0.070$ to $+0.35$ dex, and [Fe/H] shifts of $-0.055$ to $+0.13$ dex. Despite our conservative approach reducing the number of detections, we recover known trends of increasing binary fraction with higher primary mass and lower metallicity, thus reflecting the broad trends of binary populations. Accounting for unresolved binaries is essential for accurate stellar population modelling and for interpreting spectroscopic surveys--particularly in low-metallicity systems or populations with more massive stars.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, Volume 551, Issue 3, September 2026, stag1477

item.title: A Multiwavelength View of SPLUS J102139.31-282247.5: an X-ray Luminous and Eclipsing Dwarf Nova
item.description: arXiv:2610.22790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the independent discovery of the cataclysmic variable (CV) SPLUS J102139.31-282247.5 using Southern Photometric Local Universe Survey 12 band photometry, following its initial identification via ASAS-SN variability. Here, we investigate the system using optical photometry alongside optical and X-ray spectroscopy. High-cadence optical light curves from publicly available TESS data and a dedicated campaign at the Pico dos Dias Observatory in Brazil revealed a highly inclined system exhibiting pronounced eclipses with an orbital period of 1.81 hours. We found no evidence of a WD spin period. Despite seasonal gaps, the long-term ASAS-SN light curve revealed several outbursts (15 with $\Delta$mag $\sim$ 1.5 brighter than the mean magnitude) and one superoutburst over the past decade. During Swift X-ray telescope observations, the system exhibited X-ray luminosity of $8.5 \times 10^{31}$ erg s$^{-1}$ in the 0.3-10\,keV band, originating from thermal plasma emission at a temperature consistent with accretion shocks. Optical spectroscopy from the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrographs on the Gemini South telescope confirms the CV nature of the system, showing strong, double-peaked H and HeI emission lines alongside a weak HeII4686 line. Altogether, these features strongly support the classification of SPLUS J102139.31-282247.5 as a quiescent, eclipsing dwarf nova with an unusually high X-ray luminosity.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Silva de Araujo, Raimundo Lopes de Oliveira, Koji Mukai, Raymundo Baptista, Albert Bruch, Romualdo Eleuterio, Angela Krabbe, Claudia Mendes de Oliveira

item.title: Gaia in Technicolor. I. A Simple Variability-Encoded Color-Magnitude Diagram
item.description: arXiv:2610.22804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Hertzsprung-Russell diagram is one of the most important tools in stellar astrophysics. In its modern, empirical form as the Gaia color-magnitude diagram (CMD), each star is represented with a point determined from its time-averaged brightness and color. However, many stars are intrinsically variable, and the fixed-point representation ignores the variety of ways in which a star can vary. As a system pulsates, eclipses, is irradiated, erupts, or otherwise varies, it moves through the CMD along a trajectory whose size, slope, and shape are determined by the physics driving the brightness and color variability. Here we exploit the near-simultaneous, three-band, multi-epoch photometry (MEP) released for ~11.7 million sources in Gaia DR3 to construct a variability-encoded CMD (VECMD). In this updated take on the traditional CMD, each star is represented not by a point but by a linear segment approximating the path it traces in absolute magnitude and color as it varies. Because these trajectories are built from the raw epoch data, they are agnostic to period and do not require phase-folding. We show that radial-mode pulsators trace looped, Lissajous-like trajectories that can encode the phase lag between radius and temperature. The Hertzsprung bump is even visible in the CMD loops of some Cepheids. Variable binary systems can trace tight color-correlated lines and/or hooked paths. Accreting and dust-obscured systems trace long, high-amplitude tracks aligned with the outburst or reddening vector. Distinct regions of the VECMD are dominated by distinct trajectory morphologies. We argue that these trajectories are period-independent fingerprints well suited to machine learning classification, which we will pursue on the much larger epoch-photometry sample expected in Gaia DR4. Finally, we present a free app called IVECMD for finding, classifying, and analyzing variable stars in the VECMD.
item.dc:creator: Brad N. Barlow, Bennett C. Kirby

item.title: Extended J-band spectroscopy of red supergiants: parameter identifiability and metallicity robustness
item.description: arXiv:2610.23142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Red supergiants (RSGs) provide a near-infrared metallicity diagnostic complementary to optical hot-supergiant spectroscopy, but their low-resolution extragalactic use requires tests of parameter identifiability and modelling robustness. We quantify the information content of extended J-band RSG spectra at R=2000 over 1.155-1.340 um and assess recovery of effective temperature, surface gravity, microturbulence, and metallicity. Using MARCS/TURBOSPECTRUM spectra and an emulator, we perform a six-node Fisher analysis and controlled mock experiments, and analyse 21 SpeX spectra of 20 RSG candidates towards Per OB1. All four parameters produce measurable responses, but only 8-10% of the raw metallicity information and 4-7% of the gravity information are independent of the other parameter directions. Extending beyond 1.22 um provides median fractions of 60% of the raw and 66% of the nuisance-orthogonal metallicity information. Gravity dominates the weakest Fisher mode, while its prior choice shifts association means by at most 0.03 dex. Matched mocks recover metallicity with an rms error of 0.04 dex. Standard continuum treatment biases solar-metallicity mocks by about -0.23 dex, reduced to about -0.01 dex by our adopted treatment. Plausible CNO mismatch adds a zero-point sensitivity of 0.04-0.05 dex, and regularised covariance changes association means by at most 0.03 dex. The preferred analysis gives a mean [Z] = -0.10 dex with a star-to-star dispersion of 0.09 dex. Extended low-resolution J-band spectra therefore yield recoverable metallicity and temperature constraints once continuum placement and weak parameter directions are controlled, although the absolute scale remains conditional on the adopted atmosphere and line-formation framework.
item.dc:creator: M. A. Urbaneja, R. P. Kudritzki

item.title: The GAGE survey. I. Deep multi-band stellar variability characterization and automated classification toward Baade's window
item.description: arXiv:2610.23326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Context. Long-term photometric surveys of the Galactic bulge are vital for characterizing its stellar populations and structure, providing a foundation for next-generation facilities. Aims. We present initial results of the GalActic bulGe with plEiadi (GAGE) project, focusing on variable star discovery in Baade's Window. Methods. Using archival DECam (ugriz) data on the Blanco 4-m Telescope spanning six years, we applied high-precision PSF photometry. We developed a pipeline combining Generalized Lomb-Scargle analysis and polynomial light-curve modelling to derive mean multi-band magnitudes and amplitudes. Results. Quality cuts yield 6,304 high-confidence variable sources. We expand multi-band coverage for 4,568 sources in common with OGLE IV and uncover 1,736 (~28%) new candidates absent from OGLE IV. Using a Random Forest classifier, we categorize these sources, finding that 1,391 were also missing from both Gaia DR3 and VVV. This population is concentrated at the fainter end (i >= 17.5 mag), enabled by our deeper detection limits. Conclusions. Our pipeline effectively probes deep, highly crowded fields, expanding the variable star inventory of the inner Galaxy as a benchmark for Rubin-LSST.

item.title: A Neural Network - Based Tool for Rapid Orbital Solution of Contact Binary Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.23410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the rapid growth of large-scale time-domain surveys, vast amounts of photometric and spectroscopic data are continuously being released. A substantial number of contact binaries have been identified, accompanied by both light curves and radial velocity observations. Traditional modeling of these datasets relies on computationally intensive physical models, which limits their applicability to large-scale analyses. To this end, this paper proposes the use of a fully connected neural network and a SIREN (Sitzmann et al. 2020) model to rapidly generate radial velocity curves. After training, the models can rapidly generate radial velocity curves with high accuracy, significantly reducing computational costs and enabling efficient large-scale studies. This method was further integrated with the light curve computation framework developed by Li et al. (2025), allowing simultaneous fitting of radial velocities and light curves. To assess the reliability of the proposed model, synthetic observational datasets were constructed and used for parameter estimation. The deviations between the derived parameters and the ground-truth values were analyzed quantitatively, enabling a comprehensive evaluation of the model's accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Li-Heng Wang, Kai Li, Ya-Ni Guo

item.title: A Hectospec Spectroscopic Census of Kinematic Members in the Orion Nebula Cluster
item.description: arXiv:2610.23636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a comprehensive spectroscopic census of the Orion Nebula Cluster (ONC), based primarily on low-resolution optical spectroscopy obtained with MMT/Hectospec. We derive spectral types, youth indicators, and accretion diagnostics for 1513 stars located in the ONC region, enabling the identification and characterization of pre-main-sequence stars. We combine these measurements with a kinematic membership analysis based on Gaia Data Release 3 astrometry to identify and confirm cluster members. Using these combined diagnostics, we identify and characterize 780 bona fide T Tauri stars associated with the ONC. In addition, we construct a census of protoplanetary discs using infrared photometry obtained with the IRAC and MIPS instruments aboard the Spitzer Space Telescope. We further derive stellar masses, ages, and extinctions using the MassAge code, which combines photometric and spectroscopic inputs with stellar evolutionary models, and employs a Monte Carlo approach for uncertainty propagation. The resulting homogeneous catalogue of ONC members provides spectroscopic characterizations, kinematic membership constraints, disc diagnostics, and self-consistent estimates of stellar physical parameters. This dataset offers a refined view of the stellar population of the ONC and provides a robust foundation for investigating its kinematic structure, age distribution, and protoplanetary disc population.

item.title: Survey of Orion Disks with ALMA (SODA) IV: Millimeter variability of protoplanetary disks
item.description: arXiv:2610.23640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Context. Short-term millimeter-wavelength variability in Class II young stellar objects (YSOs) has been considered minimal, often dismissed as very rare in ALMA-based studies on short timescales. However, recent findings suggest that variability on sub-day timescales is significant. Aims. This study aims to quantify short timescale (~1 hour to ~3 days) millimeter flux variability in unresolved Class II YSO disks observed as part of the SODA survey, leveraging its large dataset to assess the statistical significance of such variability across the LDN 1641 and LDN 1647 regions in Orion. Methods. We analyze ALMA Band 6 observations of 873 YSOs obtained over multiple epochs using a custom flux extraction pipeline to separate individual execution blocks. By computing variability factors and statistical deviations from the mean flux, we identify sources exhibiting significant variability, accounting for noise and calibrator stability. Results. Even with conservative selection criteria, we identify 20 variable sources within the sample (~5.3% of all detections). The maximum of the measured variability factor is >=7 over about one hour. More liberal selection criteria yield up to 60 sources that could be called potentially variable (~15.9%). Conclusions. The number of variable sources detected in our sample indicates physical processes operating on time scales of hours, likely associated with magnetic reconnection and/or synchrotron radiation or strong cases of magnetic accretion changes. These detections show the need to reconsider typical stability assumptions in single-epoch observations and calls for follow-up studies in star-forming regions with ALMA. Masses derived from unresolved measurements could potentially be biased by this sort of variability.
item.dc:creator: D. Krebs, A. Hacar, J. Forbrich, S. E. van Terwisga

item.title: Characterizing the Martin Luther King Event: Sun to Earth Evolution of the January 19, 2026 Geomagnetic Storm
item.description: arXiv:2610.23704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a comprehensive Sun-to-Earth analysis of the extreme space weather event of 18 -19 January 2026, hereafter the Martin Luther King (MLK) storm, which produced a severe (G4) geomagnetic storm and one of the most intense solar radiation storms of Solar Cycle 25. The geomagnetic disturbance was driven by a fast Earth-directed coronal mass ejection (CME) associated with an X1.9-class flare from NOAA Active Region 14341. We combine multi-viewpoint remote-sensing observations, in situ measurements from Solar Orbiter and Wind, and physics-based magnetohydrodynamic simulations using the CORHEL-CME framework to reconstruct the eruption from the low corona to 1 au and identify the mechanisms governing its geoeffectiveness. Observations and simulations indicate that the eruption originated from a right-handed magnetic flux rope embedded in a complex magnetic environment dominated by a neighboring positive-polarity coronal hole. The simulations reproduce the observed CME morphology, asymmetric expansion, magnetic fields measured at both spacecraft, and Dst index evolution. The main discrepancy is attributed to filament material not included in the model. Favorable magnetic polarity alignment between the CME and coronal-hole field minimized magnetic erosion through interchange reconnection, enabling rapid escape and preservation of the strong southward magnetic field that drove the geomagnetic storm. The prolonged recovery phase resulted from interaction between the trailing CME and a following high-speed stream from the same coronal hole. These results demonstrate that storm intensity was primarily established by the coronal magnetic configuration, whereas storm duration was controlled by the ambient solar wind.
item.dc:creator: Abril Sahade, Cecilia Mac Cormack, Andreas J. Weiss, Antonio Niemela, Diego G. Lloveras, Erika Palmerio, Teresa Nieves-Chinchilla

item.title: Flashing with colours: Photometric indicators of an early interaction in type II supernovae
item.description: arXiv:2610.23852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present early-time optical photometry and spectroscopy for a sample 27 previously unpublished type II supernovae (SNe II) observed by the Precision Observations of Infant Supernova Explosions (POISE) collaboration, combined with a literature sample of 59 events to form a total sample of 86 objects. The resulting light curves comprise near-daily cadence, percent-level precision $uBgVri$ photometry. From spectra acquired within four days of the estimated explosion time, transient narrow emission lines of highly ionised elements, referred to as `flash features', can be identified. Based on the presence or absence of these lines, the SNe were categorised. We estimate key photometric properties, including rise times, peak absolute magnitude, and colour evolution. Our tests indicate that flash SNe are, on average, more luminous at the peak than their non-flash counterparts, which is consistent with previous studies. Interestingly, statistically significant differences were found in the rise times in the $B$ band, with flash SNe exhibiting a tail towards longer rise times. Flash SNe are generally bluer than non-flash events, with distinct colour distributions at 20 days post explosion, likely reflecting intrinsic differences rather than host-galaxy extinction. Colour-curve breaks within 30 days of explosion provide a clear separation between flash and non-flash SNe. The change in slopes across the break, combined with the absolute peak magnitude, yield a strong diagnostic of the flash-spectroscopic properties. This indicates that photometric observations alone may be used to identify SNe experiencing an interaction with dense circumstellar material, even in the absence of early-time spectroscopy.

item.title: Pathfinder results for populations of planet-forming discs with SKA
item.description: arXiv:2610.22456v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Imaging of few-millimetre-sized dust grains (pebbles, on the construction path to planets) in protoplanetary discs has begun. The Planet-Earth Building-Blocks Legacy e-MERLIN Survey is a unique pathfinder for SKAO, imaging a sample of disc-host stars around 4.4 cm wavelength at 55 - 120 mas resolution. PEBBLeS has surveyed 10 flux-ordered fields of the northern sky, and the L1448C-N and HL Tau systems are presented as examples. The prospects for extending this science with SKAO are bright, including shorter integration times and better sensitivity to fainter outer discs. Simulations are presented of how a southern analogue to the HL Tau disc could look to SKA-Mid AA* in bands 5a and 5b. The initial lack of long baselines is suggested to pose a significant risk for imaging of planet-related features in protoplanetary discs.
item.dc:creator: Jane S. Greaves, Anita M. S. Richards, Katie Hesterly, Emmanuel K. Bempong-Manful

item.title: The environments forming stellar and planetary systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.22462v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How does a star's birth environment set the mass, angular momentum and chemical complexity delivered to its planet-forming disk, and thereby whether it builds planets, brown dwarfs or stellar companions? This requires following material from the cloud to the sub-au to few-au scales where infalling gas, magnetized winds and the disk interact, across all star-forming environments. At frequencies where young disks are optically thin, current facilities, even ALMA after its Wideband Sensitivity Upgrade, fall short by a factor of a few in angular resolution and an order of magnitude in sensitivity. Likewise, resolving how disks around distant high-mass stars fragment into tight multiples requires a linear resolution of a few to a few tens of au, currently out of reach. Yet the disks characterized so far lie almost exclusively in nearby, isolated clouds at near-solar metallicity, although the environment (radiation field, ionization rate, gas and stellar density, pressure and metallicity) varies by orders of magnitude across the Galaxy. Most stars, probably including the Sun, form in clustered regions at kpc distances, and the widest metallicity range lies farther still, in the outer Galaxy, the Central Molecular Zone and the Magellanic Clouds. With three times finer angular resolution and ten times the sensitivity, ALMA2040 will follow the path of material from cloud to disk across the full stellar-mass spectrum and, for the first time, measure how this path changes with environment: resolving the sub-au infall-impact and wind-launching zones nearby, disk fragmentation and the onset of multiplicity in distant high-mass regions, and disk formation at a few tenths of solar metallicity. It will thereby reveal the dust-obscured, embedded origins of planetary systems that optical and infrared facilities, including the ELT, see only once they emerge, and show how the birth environment shapes them.

item.title: Contrasting geometries of kiloparsec-scale stellar flows associated with giant Galactic cavities
item.description: arXiv:2610.22488v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Giant bubbles and cavities are widespread in star-forming galactic discs, yet the stellar dynamics associated with such structures remain poorly constrained. Here we combine Gaia Data Release 3 with three-dimensional extinction information to identify 3,502 massive-star candidates corresponding to initial masses $M_{\rm ini}\gtrsim8\,M_{\odot}$ within 5 kpc of the Sun. A search of the stellar-density field alone, independent of interstellar-medium morphology and stellar kinematics, reveals two prominent overdensities, R1 and R2, with characteristic scales of approximately 1.3 kpc. Both are subsequently found to be associated with previously identified giant interstellar cavities in projected position and line-of-sight location. After subtracting locally fitted background velocity fields, stars with full three-dimensional velocities reveal coherent divergent in-plane motions across both structures. R1 extends well beyond a known massive-star association and exhibits strongly anisotropic expansion, with one principal strain rate robustly positive and the other consistent with zero. R2 instead exhibits positive strain rates along both principal directions, indicating broadly two-dimensional internal expansion. These results show that density-selected, cavity-associated stellar structures of comparable scale can host coherent kiloparsec-scale flows with contrasting internal flow geometries and need not share a common stellar kinematic organisation.
item.dc:creator: Satoya Nakano, Kengo Tachihara

item.title: Pair-exchange dynamics of magnetohydrodynamic turbulence
item.description: arXiv:2610.22729v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Nonlinear interactions in incompressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) and Navier-Stokes turbulence involve three spatial fluctuations conservatively exchanging, e.g., energy. The mathematical structure of a triad interaction does not allow to unambigously determine the specific contribution of each of the participating fluctuations to the resulting exchanges. Presently, only additional assumptions allow for the deconstruction of triad interactions into a sum of pair exchanges. This work proves that in incompressible MHD the simultaneous nonlinear transfer of cross-helicity sufficiently constrains the triad dynamics such that a mathematically unique pair-exchange representation of nonlinear energy and cross-helicity transfer is possible.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Mathieu Teissier, Wolf-Christian M\"uller

item.title: A Unified Solution to the Low-Mass X-ray Binary Diversity Puzzle: Saturated Magnetic Braking Coupled with Irradiation-Driven Winds
item.description: arXiv:2610.22816v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The standard magnetic braking (MB) model has long failed to explain key properties of low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs)---including their accretion rates, the formation of ultracompact binaries, and orbital expansion---casting doubt on binary evolution and gravitational-wave progenitor predictions. Phenomenological modifications exist, but a unified, physically grounded mechanism has been missing. Here we show that the overlooked coupling between magnetic saturation and irradiation-driven winds (IDW) provides this missing framework. Accretion-powered irradiation enhances the donor wind, which in turn amplifies MB exactly where needed. Our Saturated MB + IDW (SMB+IDW) model simultaneously resolves three outstanding discrepancies with no fine-tuning: (1) it reproduces the full observed distribution of accretion rates across persistent and transient LMXBs; (2) it naturally explains ultracompact X-ray binary formation; and (3) it quantitatively matches the orbital period distribution of descendant millisecond pulsar (MSP) binaries---a critical independent test failed by all previous models. Critically, the SMB+IDW model transforms MB from an externally imposed condition into a self-consistently regulated process tied to the accretion history. By unifying LMXB evolution to MSPs in a single physical picture, our work resolves the long-standing diversity puzzle and establishes a physics-based foundation for next-generation population synthesis, gravitational-wave progenitor predictions, and compact binary interpretation across cosmic time.
item.dc:creator: Zhu-Ling Deng, Xiang-Dong Li, Bo Wang, Philipp Podsiadlowski, Yong Shao, Dong-Dong Liu, Zhan-Wen Han

item.title: MIDSSAR: MId Dispersion Spectrograph for Stellar Activity Research
item.description: arXiv:2610.22834v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We have developed and commissioned MIDSSAR (MId Dispersion Spectrograph for Stellar Activity Research), a novel fiber-fed, dual-band spectrograph optimized for high-cadence monitoring of stellar superflares and magnetic activity phenomena, mounted on the 3.8-m Seimei Telescope at Kyoto University Okayama Observatory. Utilizing a custom-designed volume phase holographic grating and a commercially available volume binary transmission grating, the instrument achieves simultaneous observations of key chromospheric activity indicators: the CaII H&K band (382.5-406.5nm) at a resolving power of R=13,800, and the H$\alpha$ band (641.1-667.6nm) at R=18,200. MIDSSAR is strategically integrated with the existing high-dispersion spectrograph GAOES-RV to enable concurrent photosphere-chromosphere monitoring. The control software coordinates high-speed dual-camera exposures down to 1ms while incorporating real-time telescope telemetry into the data headers. We also developed a dedicated data reduction pipeline that automatically executes calibration, spatial reconstruction of the 61-fiber bundle, and one-dimensional spectral extraction with a wavelength precision of $\sim$ 0.002nm. Initial on-sky test observations conducted from March to May 2026 successfully verified the system's quantitative readiness. The observed signal-to-noise ratio characteristics perfectly align with modeled theoretical limits under varying seeing conditions, confirming that the entire instrument complex successfully meets its primary design requirements and operational expectations for systematic stellar astrophysics surveys.
item.dc:creator: Fumihde Iwamuro, Daisaku Nogami, Hiroyuki Maehara, Masaru Kino, Kai Ikuta, Akito Tajitsu, Sanghee Lee, Miho Kawabata, Keisuke Isogai, Kenta Taguchi, Kazunari Shibata

item.title: $N$-body simulations of the open cluster M67 -- I: global cluster properties
item.description: arXiv:2610.22946v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The most recent Gaia data releases have seen the construction of many open cluster catalogues containing thousands of open clusters. Simulations of these clusters are needed in order to interpret observations, both existing and upcoming. M67 is an ideal open cluster to calibrate these simulations due to its advanced age and large, diverse binary populations. Moreover it is one of the most extensively observed open clusters with observations in several wavelengths. We aim to reproduce the global cluster properties of M67 with modern $N$-body simulations, as well as comparing its observed properties in the largest homogeneous open cluster catalogue with other available observations. We carry out several NBODY6++GPU simulations with varying initial conditions, including metallicity, half-mass radius, and the distribution of orbital binary parameters. Our models broadly reproduce the observed global properties of M67, and we are able to recreate the cluster's surface brightness profile, radial mass profile, and colour-magnitude diagram. Our favoured model indicates an initial half-mass radius of around 1.6 pc, although its total observable cluster mass may be too high. Further simulations are planned for a subsequent study, with a focus on recreating the present-day binary populations of M67.
item.dc:creator: Jasmine S. M. Anderson-Baldwin, Jarrod R. Hurley

item.title: Andreev Beta Conversion and Bulk Viscosity in Superfluid Neutron-Star Matter
item.description: arXiv:2610.23581v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bulk viscosity in neutron-star matter is attributed to the phase lag between a density oscillation and weak beta equilibration. We point out a distinct coherent channel when the baryonic component that stores the condensate is superfluid: an effective beta-conversion event between a neutron condensate and normal protons can proceed as an Andreev process, converting a particle-like excitation into a hole-like excitation while adding or removing a Cooper pair from the condensate. The resulting Andreev contribution to beta equilibration is fourth order in the effective conversion vertex, is enhanced by anomalous neutron Green's functions, and is not captured by standard Urca process. We identify the density, temperature, and oscillation-frequency regimes where this channel can dominate viscous damping of neutron-star oscillations and mergers.
item.dc:creator: Tingyu Zhang, Honoka Hoshino, Hiroyuki Tajima, Motoi Tachibana, Mariusz Sadzikowski

item.title: New catalog of distances to planetary nebulae based on Gaia parallaxes and statistical distances
item.description: arXiv:2403.04606v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We have developed a method to determine the most reliable distances for a large group of planetary nebulae. For this purpose, we analyze the distances obtained from \textit{Gaia} parallaxes and three determinations of statistical distances. The most reliable distance is derived for 2211 objects, and uncertainties for these distances are calculated in a homogeneous way. Using our most reliable distances, we compare the distributions of Galactic heights of hydrogen-poor and hydrogen-rich central stars of planetary nebulae. We find that [WR] central stars are closer to the Galactic plane than hydrogen-rich central stars and than other hydrogen-poor central stars. The latter have a similar distribution to hydrogen-rich central stars, which is significantly different from the one of [WR] central stars. This result disagrees with the proposed evolutionary sequence for hydrogen-poor central stars.
item.dc:creator: Diego Hern\'andez-Ju\'arez, M\'onica Rodr\'iguez, Miriam Pe\~na

item.title: The Effect of Mass Loss and Convective Overshooting on the Pre-Collapse Structure, Composition, and Neutrino Emission of Red Supergiants
item.description: arXiv:2604.22605v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Prior to core collapse, the neutrino emission from red supergiants (RSGs) is so large that a nearby ($\lesssim1\:$kpc) RSG will become visible in current and near-future neutrino detectors. The rate of emission and the spectra of the pre-supernova (pre-SN) neutrinos from RSGs are sensitive to the temperature, density, and detailed isotopic composition of the core. During the last year of the star's life, these properties change considerably as the nuclear burning accelerates and deleptonization begins. Uncertainties in stellar evolution modeling - including the treatment of mass loss and convective overshooting - alter the thermal conditions and composition of the RSG core as it approaches collapse, and thus one expects a consequent effect upon the pre-SN emission. In this paper we present the first study of how varying the treatment of mass loss and convective overshooting together affects the pre-collapse core properties and neutrino emission of RSGs. We use the stellar evolution instrument MESA and construct a grid of 32 RSG models with zero-age main sequence masses of $\{ 12, 15, 18, 20\}$ M$_\odot$, apply the so-called "Dutch" mass-loss scheme with wind efficiencies of $\{0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 1.0\}$, and consider two convective overshooting schemes. Our models use a large 206-isotope nuclear network in order to accurately compute the structure and composition of the star. We find that varying the treatment of mass loss and overshooting results in significant differences in core properties and the strength and timing of shell burning episodes, and that the onset of silicon shell burning leads to a localized peak in the pre-SN neutrino event rate observed by a JUNO-like detector $\sim 10$ hours to $\sim 1$ hour prior to collapse.
item.dc:creator: McKenzie A. Myers, Claire B. Campbell, Kelly M. Patton, Segev BenZvi, Marta Colomer Molla, Alec Habig, James P. Kneller, Dan Milisavljevic, Jeffrey Tseng

item.title: Bifrost spectral inversions: Fast non-LTE solar chromospheric diagnostics from 3D simulations
item.description: arXiv:2608.26629v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modern solar observatories produce vast amounts of detailed spectral data. To infer atmospheric parameters from these data, in particular for the solar chromosphere, requires immense computational resources. This problem is becoming more acute as spatial resolution improves, and faster methods are much needed to make sense of the data. Archive-based inversions provide a cost-effective way to infer atmospheric parameters from solar spectra; they involve building databases of synthetic spectra and atmospheric models. We extended this idea to a k-nearest neighbour inversion with non-LTE chromospheric spectra from a 3D radiative-magnetohydrodynamic simulation. Our database consists of 150 million Ca II 8542 {\AA} line profiles from a magnetically quiet simulation. We validated our method on a different simulation and then applied the database inversion to high-cadence observations taken with the Swedish 1-m Solar Telescope. We find excellent agreement between the observed and fitted spectra for almost the entire field of view. We recovered the chromospheric temperature and line-of-sight velocity and calculated the uncertainty in their inversions. The gas temperature has small uncertainties over a broad range of optical depths, and we recover a physically consistent solution, even beyond the line sensitivity region. Compared with the traditional inversion method, our approach is four orders of magnitude faster. Limitations and future improvements of the method are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Elias R. Udn{\ae}s, Tiago M. D. Pereira, Ignasi J. Soler Poquet, Luc Rouppe van der Voort

item.title: Hydrodynamic instabilities in long-term three-dimensional simulations of neutrino-driven supernovae of 13 red supergiant progenitors
item.description: arXiv:2511.11796v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present long-term three-dimensional (3D) simulations of Type-IIP supernovae (SNe) for 13 non-rotating, single-star, red-supergiant (RSG) progenitors with zero-age-main-sequence masses between 12.5 M$_{\odot}$ and 27.3 M$_{\odot}$. The explosions were modelled with a parametric treatment of neutrino heating to obtain defined energies, ${}^{56}$Ni yields, and neutron-star properties in agreement with previous results. Our 3D SN models were evolved from core bounce until 10 days to study how the large-scale mixing of chemical elements depends on the progenitor structure. Rayleigh-Taylor instabilities (RTIs), which grow at the (C+O)/He and He/H interfaces and interact with the reverse shock forming after the SN shock has passed the He/H interface, play a crucial role in the outward mixing of ${}^{56}$Ni into the hydrogen envelope. We find most extreme ${}^{56}$Ni mixing and the highest maximum ${}^{56}$Ni velocities in lower-mass (LM) explosions despite lower explosion energies, and the weakest ${}^{56}$Ni mixing in the 3D explosions of the most massive RSGs. The efficiency of radial ${}^{56}$Ni mixing anti-correlates linearly with the helium-core mass and correlates positively with the magnitude of a local maximum of $\rho r^3$ in the helium shell. This maximum causes shock deceleration and therefore facilitates high growth factors of RTI at the (C+O)/He interface in the LM explosions. Therefore fast-moving ${}^{56}$Ni created by the asymmetric neutrino-heating mechanism is carried into the ubiquitous RT-unstable region near the He/H interface and ultimately far into the envelopes of the exploding RSGs. Our correlations may aid improving mixing prescriptions in 1D SN models and deducing progenitor structures from observed SN properties..
item.dc:creator: Beatrice Giudici (Universitat de Val\`encia), Michael Gabler (Universitat de Val\`encia), Hans-Thomas Janka (Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics, Garching)

item.title: Chemical Demographics of Star-forming Regions
item.description: arXiv:2610.22303v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Our understanding of complex organic chemistry during the formation of stars and planets is shaped by a handful of cherry-picked sources with bright molecular emission lines. This observational bias impedes our assessment of how universal chemical complexity is during star formation. The lack of systematic wideband spectral surveys for statistically significant samples of protostars and cores is a major roadblock to properly probing how COM inventories and abundances depend on the vast range of physical conditions, local cloud and global galactic environments, and evolutionary timescales of low- and high-mass star formation. In turn, this limits our ability to constrain and test physicochemical models, which depend critically on these parameters. The next-generation ALMA2040, with a 10x improvement in line sensitivity, is required to observe COMs, that we perceive as common today, in a fraction of the observing time that is needed today with ALMA. Such capabilities will propel us into the era of chemical demographics, whereby wideband (>100 GHz) spectral surveys at high sensitivity (routinely probing COM abundances down to 0.01% relative to CH3OH) will be executed towards >1000-10000 prestellar and protostellar sources. With robust chemical inventories towards large source sample sizes, we will be able to probe for dependencies of chemical complexity on mass regime, feedback processes in a cluster, Galactic position, metallicity, and time-variable accretion. Only with statistically significant samples at high sensitivity will we be able to assess the ubiquity and homogeneity of COM chemistry across the protostellar mass spectrum and natal cores. Constraining the diversity and availability of such species is critical for our understanding of the chemical reservoir available for planet formation, which eventually shapes (exo)planetary atmosphere compositions.
